name: Jaddua
overview: Jaddua is a male biblical figure noted for his unique role as a non-Levite leader mentioned in Nehemiah 10:14. He is specifically named among those who sealed the covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his significance in this communal commitment. His leadership position is distinctive given his non-Levite status.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaddua, meaning "one known," is a proper name referenced in Nehemiah 10:21. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it identifies him clearly within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jaddua is a descendant of Jacob, as noted in Nehemiah 10:21. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jaddua's importance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as a non-Levite leader who participated in the sealing of the covenant in Nehemiah 10. His inclusion among the signatories underscores the communal nature of the covenant and the involvement of leaders beyond the Levitical priesthood. This highlights the broader leadership structure during the post-exilic period and the collective commitment to God's law.
